notes: Refetching singles no longer wipes the list it was refetching. The refetch deleted the saved snapshot on its first line, then fetched — and every fetch inside it failed instantly, because it called the app’s private helpers by name from outside them (fetchWithProxy, primaryArtistName, isSingleHidden) so each call threw a ReferenceError straight into the catch-all. The result was always the same: the saved singles were gone and the popup said “No singles found from pinned artists”. The snapshot is kept until a refetch actually returns something, and a fetch that fails says so instead

The refetch and the Singles button now share one saved list. The refetch saved its result under a different popup title (“✨ Singles” instead of “🎵 Singles”), so the work it did could never be found again — closing the popup and reopening it went back to the older list, or to nothing. Both paths now use the same key, so what you see is what is saved

Singles you were missing are found now. The list was built from one relevance-ranked iTunes song search per artist, which only ever returns an artist’s most relevant ~200 tracks — so a prolific artist’s older or quieter singles were simply never in the results (“I am missing songs in singles for various artists”). Each artist is now looked up two ways and the results merged: that same song search, plus the artist’s own release list, where a one-track release is a single by definition. Previews for those extra releases are resolved so their play buttons work

A per-artist refresh (the ↻ on one artist) keeps everything else. It used to write into the current screen and then throw the saved list away, so the other artists lost what they had; the refresh now updates just that artist’s rows and saves the whole list

Albums shows only albums you made. Anything the app created on its own — the old card-drag auto-save, or an album materialised just so a reorder had somewhere to live — is out of the Albums tab and out of the “Add to album” picker. They are not deleted: they still live under “Not created by you” in Manage albums, and choosing one there (or renaming, reordering or adding songs to it) makes it yours for good
Songs you file into an album by hand now mark that album as yours, so an album you have actually been using stops being treated as the app’s own grouping
